prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the nearby trail and leaf-covered ground (bright) from the more distant trees and hillside (dark), with the path extending forward and slightly uphill through the centre. No person is visible in frame 1; the people appear at roughly 20–30 m in frame 2, 12–20 m in frame 3, 7–12 m in frame 4, and about 3–5 m in frame 5, while remaining approximately 0.5–1.5 m apart. They stay ahead of the camera wearer near the centre-right of the path and become brighter and larger as the camera approaches; the final silhouettes face roughly toward the camera. A very bright, partly cropped shape at the bottom of frame 2 corresponds to the camera wearer's fingers within arm's reach, which is clearer here than in RGB, but the washed-out foreground and soft boundaries make exact distances and thin-object geometry unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies only people: none in frame 1, a very small or partly merged detection in frame 2, and two distinct people in frames 3–5. The pair remains in front of the camera wearer near the path centre, with the dark-clothed person on the left and the orange-clothed person on the right; their masks expand across time as their distance falls from roughly 20–30 m to about 3–5 m. In the final frame they are side by side, around 0.5–1 m apart, and their RGB appearance suggests that both face generally toward the camera wearer, although the masks alone do not encode gaze or orientation reliably. This map makes the number, outlines, and partial early occlusion of the people easier to distinguish than RGB, but it omits the path, trees, fallen branches, and the camera wearer's fingers, and its overlapping text and fragmented distant masks are unreliable.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black across all five frames, so it provides no body or hand skeletons and supports no direct estimate of joint positions, facing direction, gaze, reach, or limb-level occlusion. Using the aligned RGB only, the scene changes from an empty path to two people approaching or being approached ahead of the camera, ending roughly 3–5 m away and therefore still beyond the camera wearer's arm's reach; the pair are close enough to be within roughly an arm's length of each other in the last frame. The camera wearer's fingers briefly enter the lower edge of frame 2 and are within immediate reach, but no magenta hand skeleton appears. The missing detections—especially despite clearly visible people in later frames—make this map unreliable for all requested pose-specific spatial relations.
